In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.

(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Article 4

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, development and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 12

(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:

a. establishing networks for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing I a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education I on violence against women and children; and
d. socialization ! of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 21

(1) P2TP2A reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 8

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by P2TP2A. } Article 9

• (1) P2TP2A as referred to in Article 8 is established by the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regent's Decree.

Article 15

Legal protection as referred to in Article 11 letter c includes:

a. providing protection in safe houses (shelters);
b. providing assistance in legal processes; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence may be carried out by appointing guardianship in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

Coordination as referred to in Article 11 letter d, includes: a. coordinating the handling of violence cases with provincial integrated services;

b. coordinating with integrated services in other regions; c. coordinating with service provider institutions for women and children victims of violence; and

d. coordinating and consulting with the Regional Government.

Paragraph 3

Legal Protection

Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing ' services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and become mentally healthy. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children. '

29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/ or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.

Article 2 letter a

What is meant by "respect for victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights. letter b

What is meant by "gender justice and equality" is a process to be fair to men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development. letter c

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. letter d

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration. letter e

What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions for any reason or by any means, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 4

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, development and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 19

(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.

(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

• (1) P2TP2A as referred to in Article 8 is established by the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regent's Decree.

Article 21

(1) P2TP2A reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 12

(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:

a. establishing networks for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing I a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education I on violence against women and children; and
d. socialization ! of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 4

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, development and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 18

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 11 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. letter d

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration. letter e

What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions for any reason or by any means, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

Article 16

b. coordinating with integrated services in other regions; c. coordinating with service provider institutions for women and children victims of violence; and

d. coordinating and consulting with the Regional Government.

Article 12

d. socialization ! of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 12

(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:

a. establishing networks for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing I a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education I on violence against women and children; and
d. socialization ! of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

BENGKAYANG REGENCY REGIONAL REGULATION

NUMBER 4 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

6.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Bengkayang. 2. Regional Government is the Regency of Bengkayang as an element of the regional government organizer that leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region. ' 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkayang Regency. • 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Bengkayang Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 6. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government and regional government. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Child with Special Needs is a child with special characteristics different from children in general without always indicating mental, emotional or physical disability, which includes among others: blind, deaf, mentally disabled, physically disabled, emotionally disturbed, learning difficulties, behavioral disorders, gifted children, children with health disorders and disabled children. 9. Child Protection is all forms of activities to guarantee and protect children so that they can live, grow, develop and participate in humanity discrimination. optimally in accordance with dignity and honor, ' and receive protection from violence and i

10. Special protection is protection provided to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from I minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (narcotics) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and I neglect. 11. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 13. Protection I is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 15. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity I and honor, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at: preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 17. Violence is any act that results or will result in suffering and hardship either physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 18. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in suffering or hardship of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions I, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 19. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 20. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or hardship physically, sexually, psychologically and or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 21. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 22. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to the authorized institution, whereby the concerned suffers loss due to the actions of others. 23. Service is an immediate activity and action carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as ' a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 25.

Article 4

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, development and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 8

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by P2TP2A. } Article 9

• (1) P2TP2A as referred to in Article 8 is established by the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regent's Decree.

Article 19

(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.

(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Article 21

(1) P2TP2A reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing ' services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and become mentally healthy. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children. '

29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/ or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.

Article 25

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Bengkayang Regency.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

Article 19

(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.

Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing ' services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. NUMBER 4 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

(1) In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.

(3) Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

Article 21

(1) P2TP2A reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 8

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by P2TP2A. } Article 9

• (1) P2TP2A as referred to in Article 8 is established by the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of the Regional Government, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement officers, professional personnel, companion volunteers, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

(3) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regent's Decree.

Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 4

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authority of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, development and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 12

(1) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 11 letter a include:

a. establishing networks for prevention and handling of violence through coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
b. establishing I a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence;
c. organizing communication, information, and education I on violence against women and children; and
d. socialization ! of laws and regulations related to violence against women and children.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner coordinated by the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 2 letter a

What is meant by "respect for victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights. letter b

What is meant by "gender justice and equality" is a process to be fair to men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development. letter c

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. letter d

Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. 29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/ or community organizations. 30. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.

a. providing protection in safe houses (shelters);
b. providing assistance in legal processes; and

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

CONCERNING

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

As we all know, the protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays needs to receive serious attention, particularly in Bengkayang Regency in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, this is as stated in the Bengkayang Regency Medium-Term Development Plan.

This is to provide an understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially in the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children. Therefore, it is expected that especially women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Bengkayang Regency are very high on average per semester reaching 17 (seventeen) cases, this indicates that Women's Empowerment in Bengkayang Regency in handling cases of acts of violence against women and children must receive very serious handling and attention.

In connection with this, the Bengkayang Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and how to seek protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing ' services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation of prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 26. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 27. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and become mentally healthy. 28. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children. '

29. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/ or community organizations. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victim needs. 33. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.

Article 13

a. family and closest relatives;
b. community and business world; and c. educational institutions.
